title: The Fruitfulness of the Just and the Symbolism of Gilead and Manasseh
english: To bear a hundred and sixty and thirty; as God is lifted up toward the contemplative natures of the world, which are called heavens, His glory is found upon the practical earth, which is called earth.

Not otherwise are those worthy of being loved by you can only be rescued from the enemies holding them or those surrounding them by you saving with your right hand and by me interceding for them (Ps 107:7). An oath is interpreted as a symbol of work (Ps 107:8–10). The Lord, having been lifted up on the cross and having ascended, divided the works of men as to justifying some and rejecting others; for He is a just judge.

Therefore, even the place near the surface, because it is called a valley below due to the human bodies dwelling in it, is called the measurement of the dwellings of the souls inhabiting it, to provide for both the things below and these things. Indeed, He sent the heralds of truth into all the nations, so that the gospel of justification might be proclaimed.

Gilead is interpreted as migration, Manasseh as being from oblivion, and Ephraim as fruitfulness. The Savior says, 'My Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine,' meaning    migrating from evil to truth or from evil to virtue or from earth to heaven; and mine also is the one who has overcome all the oblivion of good things and has come from it.or he who comes from oblivion into memory is Manasseh, meaning having left and abandoned the oblivion in which the good things of God were forgotten.

But also the great fruitfulness of the believing nations has become a covering and a perception of the Savior; for as Paul writes to those who were benefited by him, saying they are his joy and crown (1 Thess 2:19), so also the Savior has a perception, a crown being woven for him by those bearing up righteousness and truth. And Judah is his king, not by his ruling, but by the king being made to dwell in him. Such is David, or perhaps everyone confessing on behalf of whom Judah was strengthened, meaning confession.

Moab, however, because of being a punishment for those handed over to him by the Lord, is the lion of hope. And the lion often signifies punishment among the prophets. Since punishments fall upon a good intention, they bring good hope.
I extend my footwear
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Right Hand of God and the Glory of the Son
english: A few days, being enlightened, before he betrays the truth. Being enlightened by the true light, and receiving also the oversight of this instead of himself, becoming a teacher who both remained and progressed in the truth.

The 'fathers of Judas' who fathered him for treachery (Ps 108:14a) may be those who urged him to it by the gift of silver, as well as Satan, who put it into his heart to betray the Lord, and the rulers of this age who hold its wisdom, of whom Paul says, 'For if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory' (1 Cor 2:8). And he slew him, having become the cause of his being delivered to death (Ps 108:16c).

He who is clothed in the form of the slave speaks as to the Lord the Father (Ps 108:21–23). And he says to the Lord how he will do mercy with him, benefiting those who are his body; for the things happening to his body are reckoned to himself. Therefore he says, 'Do with me for the sake of your name, since in this I have come to those whom you sent, saying, I have come in the name of the Father; because of this name do it, for your mercy is good, benefiting and full of goodness; do it, since also my heart is troubled within me.' You say 'heart,' and the apostles are his equals, the lesser ones having become believing ones who were found to be his body. Since the disciples were not scattered having been scandalized in that night, but Judas and the crowd of the Pharisees stood over to hold him, it happened that their being troubled was his heart. But even if his heart was troubled, he did not depart from him, being held by him and dwelling in his disciples. But also everyone whose heart is being troubled from thoughts or suffering, doing nothing and saying nothing according to the trouble, says, 'My heart was troubled within me.' Since, indeed, the Savior is to live always among men (for indeed he was taken up after the resurrection into the heavens), he speaks concerning human life as not permanent nor standing, like a shadow in its vanishing: 'You were cast away from me like a chaff.' For just as the chaffs are scattered away through weakness of nature.

They are tossed about; not that I, having taken on a weak life through men, was quickly driven out of weakness to be crucified, but having been taken up after the resurrection. It is possible also to say concerning all the disciples as it is said concerning Him, 'I was tossed about like locusts' (Ps 108:30-31), since, being persecuted and tossed about by those desiring evil, they are not humbled but are carried away flying upward. And all the martyrs, having been tossed about like locusts, having left the things below, pursue the prize of the high calling.

Giving the reason for confessing and praising Him, He brought [it] so that He might stand at the right hand of the poor; it is evident regarding Him who became poor for all, that through my poverty they might become rich. He stands at the right hand of Him who does all things rightly and thinks [all things] rightly. Again, the God, having set the pretext of standing at His right hand, says, 'To save my soul' (Ps 109:1).

Having fulfilled the economy, both having been raised from the dead and having been taken up into heaven, the Lord Jesus says, 'Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet' (Ps 109:6), that is, the Father. Paul, therefore, says that after this ascension, the voice was spoken through [Him] to say, 'Having made a cleansing of sins, He sat in the right hand of majesty in the high places.' For to which of the angels was it ever said, 'Sit at my right hand?' (Heb 1:8).

The Lord, therefore, who is the Father of all those having been brought forth with Him, says to the Lord of creation, 'Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.' And the Father says to the Son, as if a father to a son and a son to a father, for He does not converse using speech; for He is His own thought, truth, wisdom, and word. And the Lord of the Lord sits in the right hands.

It is not locally, in the body, that He says these things, as if we were seeking the right hand in a place. Rather, those partaking of God are indeed in the right hand, since God is holy and good; no one else will be counted holy, reigning with the Father. For the 'Sit at my right hand' declares the co-reigning of the Son toward the Father. If it is regarding the rational [beings]: those having wisdom and the most keen virtue are thrones of God; and in these, the Savior sits at the right hand of God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The distinction between making and begetting
english: He sits. But those who have rushed toward wickedness and malice are enemies of the Word and the truth. But the Father also wills these to be changed through repentance, making them followers of the path and the feet of the Word, since having become his footstool, they fall from his feet; but with a turning toward virtue and wisdom, becoming more mobile, they themselves shall become a throne from [being] a footstool. Therefore Paul says, 'For he must reign until he has put all enemies under his feet' (Ps 110:1). And there God says, 'Until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet' (Ps 110:1). For he indeed sits at the right hands of the Father reigning, while the enemies oppose him. But having set for them the beginning of benefit by subduing them and making them his footstool, he raises their desiring hand, so that they themselves might be counted among the right-handed, no longer in the wickedness through which they happened to be on the left; so that in the end, the Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father, and all the rational beings, having been perfected, become toward the Father and the Son of God, all things becoming in all things.

Thoughts and not thus: the name of the beginning, 'kingdom,' here signifies not as with the Savior in the day of his power, but after the resurrection in which he rose from the dead; for if he was crucified out of weakness, but lives by the power of God. It signifies the beginning kindred to him which is coming, through which he holds and rules (that is, the day of his power), not in things happening by chance, but in the brightness of the saints through which they possess [light], being illuminated and made bright by the true light, as one might say, 'Let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us.' If, however, he says 'beginning' regarding those who are beginning, according to what is signified, it is said that God prevails over every beginning, and his beginning was made at his own time; and you do not say thus, but rather those who are beginning are under him in the day of his power, when the sun of righteousness shines (Mal 4:2). For he himself says concerning those being ruled by him toward the Father, 'I want that where I am, they also may be, that they may see my glory' (Ps 110:3). All the ecclesiastics were not before now...

But they also always say that the appointed voice is said towards the Father, joined to the beginning of the psalm thus: 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, so that I may make your enemies a footstool for your feet; from the womb before the dawn I begot you' (Psalm 110:1; Psalm 89:12)—through the middle of the other half-verses.

And indeed the apostle, having followed this thought, has said: 'For which of the angels did he ever say, Sit at my right hand?' (Hebrews 1:5) saying only once. Not to any of the born, but to his only-begotten Son alone: 'Sit at my right hand,' since he himself is alone the only-begotten who is in the bosom of the Father.

Let us see also what this very word intends. And it must be said that God is indeed simple and undivided; and even while he is thus, if the divine Word wishes to truly present himself as a maker, from whom we are, he says, speaking of his hands, that the heavens and the rest of creation are the work of his hands.

Just so, with genuine parents, whom we call a star, if we mean not the adoptive ones but the genuine ones, since some are truly sons and others are adoptive and placed; if we do not mean the placed ones but the genuine ones, we say they are the offspring of the womb of those who bore them. And God, wishing to present a genuine Son and the only-begotten from himself, remembers the womb.

But just as he makes it with hands in a God-befitting way, so also we hear 'to have been begotten from the womb.' But the works of the hands are many, while the only-begotten offspring of the womb is one; therefore, it is not to be said of God that creating and begetting are the same, as some say.

For all things were made through the Word and in wisdom (John 1:3), and the wisdom and the Word were not through something, but were begotten from God. Therefore, begetting is not the same as making; for if there were no difference, nothing would prevent saying: 'My hands made you, and the heavens are the work of my womb.'

But just as the word has many variations, so also the things signified by it. But the Father does not say these things to the Son in ignorance, but so that we might know the intimacy of the Father toward the Son and of the Son toward the Father, these things were written. Just as what was said by that same only-begotten Wisdom: 'Before all mountains he begets me' (Proverbs 8:25), therefore also there, before the dawn...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
